w10_T4_001680: Maya arrived at the car-boot sale with 196 second-hand books in the boot of her car. By noon she had sold 163 of them. She then threw away 8 more whose covers had come apart in the rain. Her brother Nolan, who had brought far fewer books than Maya, passed her 20 of his own to sell. A neighbour added 33 paperbacks to Maya's table after that. Maya has been running this stall for a dozen weekends. How many books does Maya have on her table now?
w10_T4_001681: A parcel depot began Tuesday with 124 parcels on the sorting bench. A late van brought in 69 more. Then 5 parcels were pulled out as damaged, and 44 went off on the first delivery round. Every parcel still on the bench contains 3 separately wrapped items. The drivers cover 87 kilometres on a typical round and log their journeys in minutes rather than hours. How many wrapped items are on the bench?
w10_T4_001684: Sofia counted 197 eggs in the farm's cold room on Friday morning. A restaurant order took 182 of them straight away. She then found 9 eggs cracked in their trays and threw those out. Her colleague Anton, who keeps far fewer hens than Sofia does, borrowed 2 for the staff kitchen. On Saturday the hens gave 74 more eggs, and a neighbouring farm sent 13 across as a thank-you. Anton has worked on this farm for a dozen seasons. How many eggs are in the cold room now?
w10_T4_001688: Tomas laid out 203 blank badges for the conference. He set 36 aside because the printing on them had smudged. Every badge he kept was mounted on a card carrying 4 ribbons. His colleague Nadine, who had prepared fewer badges than Tomas, brought 15 spare ribbons, and the venue supplied 30 more. During registration 626 ribbons were handed out to delegates. The conference hall seats 900 people. How many ribbons are left?
w10_T4_001694: Grace filled 96 trays for the school garden, and every tray held 4 seedlings. She and her friend Owen planted the whole lot across 4 beds, sharing them out equally, though Owen looked after fewer beds than Grace did. Every seedling in the bed Grace tends produced 4 flowers this summer. A neighbour gave her another 15 flowers to go with them. The school sold each of Grace's flowers for 3 pounds at the fete, where the raffle had 250 tickets. Grace has been gardening at the school since she was a dozen years old. How many pounds did Grace's flowers raise?
w10_T4_001697: A jam co-operative started the week with 16 boxes in its store. A member delivered 66 more boxes on Tuesday, and a second member brought 77 on Thursday. Every box in the store holds 9 jars. A cafe returned 70 unsold jars, which were stacked in with the rest. Each jar contains 8 spoonfuls of jam according to the label, and the co-operative's van can carry a dozen boxes at a time. The store itself measures 45 square metres. How many spoonfuls of jam are in the store?
w10_T4_001699: A chocolate warehouse held 224 crates before the holiday rush and sent 135 of them out to shops. Every crate that stayed behind was split into 2 smaller boxes. A returning delivery added 64 more boxes of the same kind. Each box holds 8 packs, and every pack contains 6 bars. Each of those bars can be snapped into 4 squares. How many squares of chocolate does the warehouse hold?
w10_T4_001704: Isla packed 31 boxes for the craft market, and each box held 9 candles. A friend added 18 loose candles to her stock. Every candle sold for 5 pounds by the end of the day. Isla and the other stallholders then shared the takings equally between the 5 of them. Isla spent 260 pounds of her share on wax for next month, while her friend Bruno spent much less of his. The market charges 62 pounds for a pitch. How many pounds does Isla have left?
w10_T4_001711: Ravi counted 115 stamp sheets in his album and was given 7 more by his uncle. He then removed 16 sheets that were torn at the perforations. Every sheet he kept carries 4 stamps. His friend Tessa, whose collection is smaller than Ravi's, gave him 62 loose stamps from her own album. A dealer sold him another 71 loose stamps that afternoon. Ravi's catalogue prices everything in cents rather than dollars. How many stamps does Ravi have now?
w10_T4_001712: A stadium kiosk took delivery of 221 trays of pies before the final. Each tray carried 5 boxes, and every box held 3 pies. Before kick-off the kiosk sold 412 pies to early arrivals. During the first half another 1735 pies went over the counter, and at half-time a further 529 were sold. The kiosk keeps a dozen staff on duty for a match like this, and the stadium itself holds 48000 spectators. How many pies are left in the kiosk?
w10_T4_001715: Farid harvested 231 sacks of potatoes, and his cousin Amira, who farms a smaller field, added 71 sacks of her own to the pile. Every sack in the combined pile holds 8 kilograms. A late load added 15 kilograms of loose potatoes to the same pile. The market rejected 103 kilograms as too small and sent them elsewhere. A restaurant then returned 40 kilograms it could not use. How many kilograms of potatoes are in the pile now?
w10_T4_001718: In the morning a print shop ran off 168 posters on each of its 6 machines. Before lunch a courier delivered 56 posters printed elsewhere, and they joined the same stack. During the afternoon 261 posters were pasted up around the town. In the evening a cancelled order sent 56 posters back to the stack. The shop's front window is 3 metres wide. How many posters are on the stack at the end of the day?
w10_T4_001720: A label printer packed 45 crates, and each crate held 6 packets. A late order added 54 more packets of the same kind. Every packet contains 4 sheets, and each sheet is printed with 9 labels. The whole stock was divided equally between 4 branches, and the Riverside branch took one of those equal shares. The delivery van has covered 78000 kilometres, and the firm has been trading for a dozen years. How many labels went to the Riverside branch?
w10_T4_001721: Nina printed 235 raffle tickets for the village hall. She gave 108 of them to the school to sell, and a further 40 were spoiled when the printer jammed. Her co-organiser Sam, who handled fewer tickets than Nina did, sold every remaining ticket at 5 dollars each. The hall's hire and the prizes together cost 369 dollars, paid straight out of that money. The takings were counted in cents at the door and written up afterwards in dollars. How many dollars were left for the village fund?
w10_T4_001725: Kofi brought 47 flat-pack shelf kits to the workshop, and his partner Delia, who brought slightly fewer than he did, added 44 kits of her own. Every kit in the order needs 9 brackets. Each bracket is fixed with 2 bolts. Every bolt comes in a bag with 6 washers. Each washer is pressed from 2 thin metal discs. How many discs does the whole order use?
w10_T4_001727: Yusuf counted 187 folding chairs in the hall store, rather more than his assistant Mrs. Adeyemi had counted the week before. A wedding party took 157 of them out to the marquee. The caretaker then returned 5 chairs that had not been needed. Every chair still in the store was hired out to a choir at 5 pounds each. Mending a broken table cost the hall 158 pounds, paid straight out of that hire money. Yusuf has looked after this hall for a dozen years. How many pounds were left from the hire money?
w10_T4_001733: Elena knitted 63 blanket squares in each of 9 weeks. She had to unravel 18 of them because the colours clashed badly. Her friend Piotr, who knits more slowly than Elena, contributed 77 squares to the same blanket. Every square in the finished blanket took 5 metres of wool. The charity shop that will sell it opens at half past eight and has 240 members on its mailing list. How many metres of wool went into the blanket?
w10_T4_001734: Farah counted 200 beads in her tin and then found 7 more under the table. Each bead is worth 5 cents at the craft shop, so she worked out the value of the whole tin in cents rather than dollars. She divided that value equally between 3 charity jars. Her brother Idris, who had saved less than she had, added 69 cents to the jar Farah had filled first. Farah has been beading since she was a dozen years old. How many cents are in that jar now?
w10_T4_001745: A cafe received 15 crates of juice, and each crate contained 3 bottles. During the lunch rush 20 of those bottles were emptied. A clumsy delivery then smashed another 16 bottles out in the yard. Every bottle still standing fills exactly 6 glasses. The barista poured 3 more glasses from a jug that had been left in the fridge. The cafe seats 42 people and prints its opening times in minutes past the hour rather than in hours. How many glasses of juice are there in total?
w10_T4_001748: A builder had 57 boxes of floor tiles in his van and picked up 13 more from the yard. Every box holds 4 tiles. A neighbour gave him 72 loose tiles left over from her kitchen, and the merchant threw in 51 more as a goodwill gesture. Laying the hallway and the bathroom used up 327 tiles. The van is 6 metres long, and the builder quotes his jobs in days rather than in hours. How many tiles does the builder have left?
w10_T4_001749: A conference centre had 170 stacking chairs and borrowed 16 more from the church hall. The chairs were shared out equally between 6 meeting rooms. From the Oak room 24 chairs were then taken away for a talk in the garden. The centre later set out 4 side rooms so that each one matched the Oak room exactly, chair for chair. The car park outside holds 95 vehicles. How many chairs were set out in those 4 side rooms altogether?
w10_T4_001750: A garden centre started the morning with 174 crates of bedding plants and sent 162 crates off to a landscaping job. Each crate still on site holds 6 pots. A local school returned 61 pots it had not planted after all. A supplier then delivered 76 more pots to the same bench. The centre's price labels are printed in pence rather than pounds. How many pots are on the bench now?
w10_T4_001757: A recycling depot began the week with 194 sacks and took in 56 more on Monday. A caretaker found 4 further sacks behind the bins. Over the next fortnight the depot's sack count grew to 2 times what it had been at that point. A school then delivered another 26 sacks after its big clear-out. Every sack in the depot holds 7 flattened boxes, and a passing driver handed in 33 loose boxes at the gate. The depot's weighbridge can take 40 tonnes. How many flattened boxes does the depot hold?
w10_T4_001758: A hotel laundry started the day with 228 towels on the rack. Housekeeping took 78 of them upstairs to the guest rooms. A delivery from the supplier then added 72 fresh towels to the same rack. Every towel now on that rack is cut into 4 cleaning cloths. Each cloth is finished with 6 stitched loops around its edge. How many stitched loops will the whole rack need?
w10_T4_001759: A campsite had 36 tent pegs in the store hut. The warden bought 68 more from the outdoor shop, and a departing group left 50 behind. Each peg is wrapped in 5 turns of tape before it goes into a kit bag. Every turn of tape uses 6 centimetres from the roll. The campsite has 24 pitches beside the river. How many centimetres of tape are needed in total?
